standard.title: Country/Place and First Nations Australians
standard.description: the importance of Country/Place to First Nations Australians and the Country/Place on which the school is located
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have general experience of place from AC9HSFK03. No formal prior knowledge of First Nations Australian concepts of Country/Place.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the importance of Country/Place to First Nations Australians, name the local First Nations Australian language group, and identify the Country/Place on which their school is located.

nodes.label: What Country/Place means to First Nations Australians
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why the term Country/Place (capitalised) is used by First Nations Australians and how its meaning differs from everyday uses of 'country' or 'place'.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain in simple terms that Country/Place is used by First Nations Australians to describe a deep, living connection to land, sea, waterways, sky and animals — not just a physical location.
nodes.typical_width: Explore the meaning of Country/Place through stories, invited community members, and visual sources; describe what connections First Nations Australians have to Country/Place (land, sea, sky, living things, spiritual connections).
wider: Listen to and respond to Dreaming and Creation stories that describe the relationship between First Nations Australians and specific Country/Place features
Compare the concept of Country/Place with students' own experiences of places that feel special or belonging to them
nodes.hinge_reason: Without understanding the distinct meaning of Country/Place, students cannot identify the local language group or discuss local significance in Node 2 — the conceptual distinction is necessary before applying it locally.

response_modes.reason: The concept of Country/Place as a living relationship (not just a physical location) requires explicit scaffolding. Use concrete anchors — stories, images, community voices — before asking students to explain the concept.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The concept of Country/Place connects to geography, history, spirituality and identity — engaging with it richly at Foundation sets a foundation for all subsequent First Nations content across the curriculum.
success_criteria: Explains that Country/Place means more to First Nations Australians than just a physical location
Gives at least one example of a connection First Nations Australians have to Country/Place

nodes.label: Our local Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use the name of the local First Nations Australian language group and name the Country/Place on which their school is located.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the name of the local First Nations Australian language group and state the Country/Place of the school.
nodes.typical_width: Use the name of the local First Nations Australian language group correctly in context; identify local places of cultural significance to that group; listen and respond to community members talking about Country/Place.
wider: Identify multiple local places of significance to First Nations Australians in the local area
Explore how Welcome to Country and Acknowledgement of Country ceremonies are used to recognise Traditional Owners and Custodians

response_modes.reason: Local community engagement — where possible, invited Traditional Owners or community members — provides the most authentic and respectful context for this node.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Local First Nations community connections are rich and contextually specific; the local knowledge available here cannot be replicated from curriculum materials alone.
success_criteria: Names the local First Nations Australian language group
States the Country/Place on which their school is located
